emergence.summary: The commonest heritable form of rickets/osteomalacia. PHEX (a membrane endopeptidase expressed by osteocytes/osteoblasts) normally restrains the bone hormone FGF23; PHEX loss-of-function RELEASES that restraint, so circulating FGF23 is OVER-produced. Excess FGF23 downregulates the renal sodium-phosphate cotransporters (NaPi-2a/2c) and suppresses 1-alpha-hydroxylase, causing renal phosphate wasting with inappropriately low calcitriol -> hypophosphataemic rickets, bowing, short stature, dental abscesses and enthesopathy. Read as a released BRAKE on FGF23 (PHEX brakes FGF23; LOF releases it -> FGF23 burden UP) -- the same released-brake -> downstream-over-production pattern as the toxic-metabolite axis-UP diseases, here on a HORMONE axis. The kit re-derives the approved targeted therapy, which RESTRAINS the FGF23 axis: burosumab, an anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody, neutralises the excess hormone and restores renal phosphate reabsorption. Restoring PHEX itself (gene therapy preclinical) is the function-restoring lever. Conventional oral phosphate + active vitamin D (calcitriol/alfacalcidol) is the older symptomatic standard that repletes the downstream phosphate/calcitriol deficit but does NOT lower FGF23 (it can raise it), so it sits OUTSIDE this FGF23 switch axis and is noted as downstream-symptomatic, not a switch lever. The gamma read is of the PHEX locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesion is coding/deletion (loss-of-function variants across PHEX), outside the promoter firewall. X-linked dominant (Xp22.11); the link PHEX-loss -> FGF23-excess is functionally established while the precise enzymatic substrate is still investigated. Magnitude [O].

per_gene.note: PHEX (phosphate-regulating endopeptidase, X-linked) is expressed by osteocytes/osteoblasts and functionally RESTRAINS circulating FGF23. As a BRAKE on FGF23, its LOF RELEASES the brake -> FGF23 is over-produced -> renal phosphate wasting + low calcitriol -> the FGF23 hormone burden goes UP. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the coding/deletion lesion (firewall). The pathological axis is the FGF23 BURDEN (it goes UP), so the corrective lever LOWERS it. X-linked dominant (Xp22.11).

falsifiers.claim: PHEX LOF (released brake) raises circulating FGF23 and drives renal phosphate wasting (axis UP)
falsifiers.falsifier: a PHEX loss-of-function variant that LOWERED circulating FGF23 / RAISED serum phosphate would refute the released-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: circulating intact FGF23 and renal phosphate handling (TmP/GFR) by PHEX genotype

falsifiers.claim: neutralising the excess FGF23 (burosumab) is the CORRECTIVE direction (restores phosphate, lowers the burden)
falsifiers.falsifier: if an anti-FGF23 antibody FAILED to raise serum phosphate / TmP/GFR, or worsened phosphate wasting, the restrain-FGF23 lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: serum phosphate and TmP/GFR response to an anti-FGF23 antibody
